object.title: The $\frac{3\pi}{2}$-open spanning path conjecture
object.statement:
Let $S$ be a finite point set in general position in the plane. A spanning path of $S$ is a plane straight-line path containing every point of $S$. Such a path is **$\alpha$-open** when all angles relevant to its openness are at most $\alpha$.

**$\frac{3\pi}{2}$-open spanning path conjecture.** Every finite point set in general position in the plane has a $\frac{3\pi}{2}$-open spanning path.

This is the paper's concluding formulation of the conjectured bound for spanning paths in general position. The paper establishes a non-tight bound of $\frac{5\pi}{4}$ and leaves the stated existence claim unresolved.

object.title: Uniqueness conjecture for non-cyclic graphs of finite non-abelian simple groups
object.statement:
For a group $G$, let $\Gamma_G$ be its non-cyclic graph, whose vertices are the elements outside

$$
Cyc(G)=\{x\in G\mid \langle x,y\rangle\text{ is cyclic for all }y\in G\},
$$

and whose edges join pairs of vertices that do not generate a cyclic subgroup. **Uniqueness conjecture.** If $M$ is a finite non-abelian simple group and $\Gamma_M\cong\Gamma_G$ for some group $G$, then $G\cong M$. This is the paper's concluding conjecture, extending the proved cases and asserting that the non-cyclic graph recognizes every finite non-abelian simple group; the general claim remains open in the supplied text.

object.statement:

$$
S_-(X)=\{Y\subset X:\operatorname{rank}(X\setminus(Y\cup\{x\}))=n\text{ for every }x\in X\setminus Y\}.
$$

Let ${\cal P}_-(X)$ be the internal ${\cal P}$-space. **Very short sets conjecture.** For every $X$,

$$
{\cal P}_-(X)=\operatorname{span}\{p_Y:Y\in S_-(X)\}.
$$

object.title: Stabilizer characterization conjecture for faces of permutation polytopes
object.statement:
Let $G\leq S_n$ be a permutation group, let $H\leq G$ be a subgroup, and let $P(G)$ and $P(H)$ denote the associated permutation polytopes. For a partition

$$
[n]:=\{1,\ldots,n\}=\bigsqcup_i I_i,
$$

write

$$
\operatorname{stab}(G;(I_i)_i):=\{\sigma\in G:\sigma(I_i)=I_i\text{ for all }i\}\leq G.
$$

**Stabilizer characterization conjecture.** If $P(H)\preceq P(G)$ is a face, then

$$
H=\operatorname{stab}(G;(I_i)_i)
$$

for some partition $[n]=\bigsqcup_i I_i$.

The paper notes that stabilizers of partitions provide an obvious class of subgroups whose permutation polytopes are faces. The conjecture asks whether every subgroup yielding a face arises this way; its resolution is not given.

object.title: The exterior face algebra characterization for tree braid groups
object.statement:
Let $T$ be a tree, let $B_nT$ denote the braid group on $n$ strands on $T$, and let $H^*(B_nT)$ denote its cohomology ring. An **exterior face algebra** is the exterior face algebra structure on this cohomology ring.

**Exterior face algebra conjecture.** $H^*(B_nT)$ is an exterior face algebra if and only if $n<6$ or $T$ is linear.

The authors have established the forward cases when $n<6$ or $T$ is linear; the converse is conjectured and concerns the absence of an exterior face algebra structure for all remaining tree braid groups.

object.title: Elizalde–Noy maximality conjecture for consecutive pattern avoidance
object.statement:
Let $S_k$ denote the set of permutations of length $k$, and let $alpha_p(n)$ be the number of permutations of length $n$ avoiding the consecutive pattern $p$. For a fixed pattern length $k$, write

$$
sigma=1 2 ldots k.
$$

**Elizalde–Noy maximality conjecture.** The increasing pattern $\sigma$ is the maximal pattern, in the sense that

$$
\alpha_{\sigma}(n) \geq \alpha_p(n)
$$

for all $p\in S_k$ and all $n$. This conjecture concerns the extremal enumeration of consecutive pattern avoidance; the source attributes it to Elizalde and Noy and gives no resolution.

object.statement:

\mathcal{C}(G_i,S_i)

object.title: Conjecture on the limiting distribution of random Cayley graph diameters
object.statement:
Let $q$ be prime, let $g_1,\ldots,g_k$ be independent uniformly random generators of the cyclic group ${\mathbb Z}_q$, and let $Diam(q,k)$ denote the diameter of the resulting directed Cayley graph. The same notation may be used for the corresponding undirected Cayley graph with generating set $\{g_1,-g_1,\ldots,g_k,-g_k\}$. **Diameter distribution conjecture.** The normalized diameter

$$
\frac{Diam(q,k)}{\sqrt[k]{q}}
$$

converges in distribution to some distribution $D(k)$ on ${\mathbb R}$ whose support is non-compact. The preceding upper and lower bounds show that the normalization by $\sqrt[k]{q}$ is of the correct order and that the limiting behavior is non-degenerate in the stated sense; the existence and non-compactness of the limiting distribution remain open in the source.

object.title: Guo–Zeng's gamma-positivity conjecture for involution descent polynomials
object.statement:
Let $\mathcal{I}_n$ be the set of involutions in $\mathfrak{S}_n$, and define

$$
I_n(t)=\sum_{\pi\in\mathcal{I}_n}t^{\operatorname{des}(\pi)}.
$$

**Guo–Zeng conjecture.** For every $n\in\mathbb{N}$, there exist coefficients $a_{n,i}\in\mathbb{N}$ such that

$$
I_n(t)=\sum_{i=0}^{\lfloor (n-1)/2\rfloor}a_{n,i}t^i(1+t)^{n-1-2i},
$$

where $0\leq i\leq\lfloor (n-1)/2\rfloor$.

This is a gamma-positivity expansion for the descent polynomial of involutions. The source presents it as an open problem after noting that unimodality and symmetry were already known.

object.title: The no-accumulation-from-above conjecture for ordered graph speeds
object.statement:
Let $\mathcal{S}$ be the set of exponential growth constants arising from hereditary properties of ordered graphs. For each real number $c$, consider the interval immediately to its right.

**No-accumulation-from-above conjecture.** For every $c\in\mathbb{R}$, there exists $\varepsilon=\varepsilon(c)$ such that

$$
\mathcal{S}\cap(c,c+\varepsilon)=\emptyset.
$$

In particular, $\mathcal{S}$ has no accumulation points from above.

This is the proposed general “jump everywhere” principle for the possible exponential speeds. The supplied text gives no resolution.
